proof:
Source: fact (F1) of the parent proof, second half: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2) ("by taking a C⁰ function f : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → [0,1] with f ≡ 1 in B_1(0) and f ≡ 0 off B_{1+ε}(0), the definition (∗) implies lim_{ρ↓0} (ω_n ρⁿ)⁻¹∫_{M ∩ B_ρ(y)} θ dHⁿ = θ(y)"), with the matching lower bound obtained in the same way from a function equal to 1 on B_{1-ε}(0) and 0 off B_1(0).
Setting: n ≥ 1, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} open, V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U, M := V.carrier, θ := V.mult, Hⁿ := μHE[n], μ := V.weight, x ∈ U, and P with Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P: finrank P = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^{n+ℓ}, ℝ), I_r(f) := ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y)·θ(x + ry) dHⁿ(y) → θ(x)·∫_P f dHⁿ as r ↓ 0, where η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y - x). Goal: V.HasDensity x θ(x).
1. Choose d > 0 with B_{2d}(x) ⊆ U (U open). The closed ball B_{2d}(x) is compact, so θ is integrable on M ∩ B_{2d}(x).
2. Change of variables. η_{x,r} is a translation followed by the homothety of ratio r⁻¹, so Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(A)) = r⁻ⁿHⁿ(A) for every A (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀ and translation invariance of μHE[n]); equivalently, the pushforward of Hⁿ⌞M under η_{x,r} is rⁿ·Hⁿ⌞η_{x,r}(M). Hence for 0 < r ≤ d and every measurable g : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → [0, 1] vanishing off B_2(0): ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} g(y)θ(x + ry) dHⁿ(y) = r⁻ⁿ∫_M g(η_{x,r}(z))θ(z) dHⁿ(z), a finite integral (only z ∈ M ∩ B_{2r}(x) ⊆ M ∩ B_{2d}(x) contribute). For g = 1_{B_1(0)} (closed unit ball), η_{x,r}(z) ∈ B_1(0) ⟺ z ∈ B_r(x), so J_r := ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} 1_{B_1(0)}(y)θ(x + ry) dHⁿ(y) = r⁻ⁿ∫_{M ∩ B_r(x)} θ dHⁿ, and μ(B_r(x)) = ∫⁻_{M ∩ B_r(x)} ofReal θ dHⁿ = ofReal(rⁿ J_r) (θ > 0 on M, integrable there).
3. Test functions. For ε ∈ (0, 1) let f_ε(y) := min(1, max(0, (1 + ε - ‖y‖)/ε)) and g_ε(y) := min(1, max(0, (1 - ‖y‖)/ε)). Both are continuous with compact support (f_ε = 0 off B_{1+ε}(0), g_ε = 0 off B_1(0)), take values in [0, 1], f_ε = 1 on B_1(0), g_ε = 1 on B_{1-ε}(0); hence g_ε ≤ 1_{B_1(0)} ≤ f_ε. Since θ > 0 on M, the integrands are ≥ 0 on η_{x,r}(M), and for 0 < r ≤ d/2: I_r(g_ε) ≤ J_r ≤ I_r(f_ε).
4. Plane integrals. Hⁿ⌞P is the n-dimensional Lebesgue measure of the n-dimensional subspace P (normalization of μHE[n] and isometry invariance), so Hⁿ(P ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_n sⁿ for s ≥ 0 (simongmt Chapter04 planeMeasure_unit_closedBall with scaling). Hence ∫_P f_ε dHⁿ ≤ Hⁿ(P ∩ B_{1+ε}(0)) = ω_n(1 + ε)ⁿ and ∫_P g_ε dHⁿ ≥ Hⁿ(P ∩ B_{1-ε}(0)) = ω_n(1 - ε)ⁿ > 0.
5. θ(x) ≥ 0: I_r(g_ε) ≥ 0 for small r and I_r(g_ε) → θ(x)∫_P g_ε dHⁿ with ∫_P g_ε dHⁿ > 0.
6. By the hypothesis and steps 3-5: limsup_{r↓0} J_r ≤ lim I_r(f_ε) = θ(x)∫_P f_ε ≤ θ(x)ω_n(1 + ε)ⁿ and liminf_{r↓0} J_r ≥ lim I_r(g_ε) = θ(x)∫_P g_ε ≥ θ(x)ω_n(1 - ε)ⁿ. Letting ε ↓ 0 gives J_r → θ(x)ω_n, i.e. μ(B_r(x))/(ω_n rⁿ) → θ(x) in ℝ (the real ratio equals J_r/ω_n).
7. For 0 < r ≤ d, μ(B_r(x)) = ofReal(rⁿJ_r) < ∞ and 0 < ω_n rⁿ, so μ(B_r(x))/ofReal(ω_n rⁿ) = ofReal(J_r/ω_n) in ℝ≥0∞ (ENNReal.ofReal_div_of_pos); by continuity of ENNReal.ofReal, μ(B_r(x))/ofReal(ω_n rⁿ) → ofReal(θ(x)) along 𝓝[>]0. This is V.HasDensity x (V.mult x).
